messages:
alex: Noticed a curious spike in p99 for /v1/generate at ~10:12 UTC on the latency dashboard. p50/p95 steady but p99 up by ~280ms. The dashboard overlay shows fallback fraction increased from ~2% -> ~35% at 10:10. Screenshot posted: https://img.redwood.internal/spike.png

maria: @alex can you paste the exact widget query/filters? trying to repro locally.

alex: Widget query: `service:inference endpoint:/v1/generate | percentile(50,95,99) by route, deployment` with `tag:fallback=true` overlay. I can also dump raw sample counts if helpful.

devon: we pushed a routing-policy change at 10:05 to enable regional fallback when eu-west reaches 85% util. That redirected some traffic to standby pools with different capacity/provisioning.

jeff: adding context: console rollups use t-digest merge (merge_mode=weighted-by-samples). If 30% of traffic moves to a smaller deployment with lower sample throughput and different latency distribution, the aggregated tdigest p99 can jump even if the primary is unchanged. Not necessarily a bug but surprising.

erica: UI/product note: origin badge currently only shows `fallback` bool; it doesn't show which deployment variant or which timestamp the weight change happened. Users have asked for outbreak annotations when route weights shift >10%.

kate: ops hypothesis: fallback traffic likely hits cold instances -> low KV cache hit -> heavy-tail. Can we get sample_count + kvcache_hit rate for the standby pool?

alex: ran quick query against traces: `select route, count(*) as n, avg(kvcache_hit) as k, pctile_latency(99) as p99 from samples where endpoint='/v1/generate' and ts between '2026-03-20T10:00:00Z' and '2026-03-20T10:20:00Z' group by route` Result: `primary: n=120000 k=0.92 p99=310ms; standby: n=60000 k=0.37 p99=590ms`.

maria: matches expectations. Standby pool much lower kvcache_hit and much higher tail. Console aggregates endpoint-level p99 by merging t-digests, so endpoint p99 reflects combined distribution.

jeff: two problem areas: (1) telemetry provenancewe need clearer breakdown by route/deployment when rollouts/fallbacks occur; (2) SLO/alert semanticstdigest merge can mask that a small subpopulation has a much higher tail.

devon: short-term: add an annotation on the latency widget showing `fallback weight -> standby: 35% at 10:05`. Also surface per-route sample-count inline so users can see the split at a glance. Long-term: add alternative rollup modes (e.g., `max(child_p99s)` vs `tdigest_merged_p99`).

erica: UX experiment idea: default to `endpoint view` but show a compact route-breakdown pill if p99 increases >20% within 15m and correlates with a >10% traffic shift. I'll mock a quick UI with the pill and an expand-to-breakdown interaction.

kate: ops immediate action: create dashboard alert for `kvcache_hit < 0.5` per pool and link to the rollout that triggered fallback. Add runbook step: if fallback weight >25% and p99 delta >200ms, escalate to oncall.

alex: repro query for devs: ```
# sample counts by route
SELECT route, count(*) FROM samples
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND time >= '2026-03-20T10:00:00Z' AND time < '2026-03-20T10:30:00Z'
GROUP BY route;
```

maria: one more thought: when merging subpopulation t-digests we could also expose a secondary metric `p99_max_children = max(child_p99)` and surface both `p99_td` and `p99_max`. SREs can use `p99_max` for conservative SLO checks. Doable?

jeff: yes. Implement alt rollup mode `p99_max_children` in the backend and expose both in the console. Caveat: `p99_max_children` will be noisy on small-sample children; so only show if child sample_count > threshold (e.g., >500 samples in window).

devon: plan: prototype both values in the UI for 7 days. If `(p99_max_children - p99_td) > 150ms` show an attention pill. We'll evaluate false positives.

sre-bot: alert created: `kvcache-standby-low-hit` (dashboard 3421) triggered at 10:12 UTC; incident channel #incidents notified.

kate: I'll add the runbook link and post the UX mock to the tracker. Summary: not a percentile algorithm bug; root cause is provenance/UX gap + real perf difference from KV cache misses in standby pool. Actions: annotate dashboard, show per-route sample counts, prototype `p99_max_children`, add kvcache alert and runbook. :thumbsup:

alex: will follow up with a short postmortem once we've confirmed remediation. Thanks everyone.
